title: Ship a Whole Plan
bottom_line: Run /plan-tools:plan-implement-complete, answer one round of questions, and Claude implements your plan, reviews it, opens the pull request and can watch it merge.

sections.heading: Start it with your plan, or let Claude find it

blocks.caption: Without --branch, the work goes on a branch named plan/<feature-name>.

blocks.title: How Claude finds the plan
blocks.caption: A split plan is `.planning/progress.md` plus `.planning/sessions/`, written by /plan-tools:split-plan. If Claude had to guess the file, it confirms it with you.

blocks.text: The plan in this conversation might be one you just approved in plan mode. If Claude finds no plan at all, it tells you and stops.

cards.title: GitHub CLI signed in
cards.text: `git` and the GitHub CLI (`gh`), signed in with `gh auth login`, with push access to the repository. Every issue, PR and status command goes through `gh`.

cards.title: A plan to build
cards.text: A split plan in `.planning/`, or a single plan file.

terms.definition: A request on GitHub to merge a branch of code into the main code, where it can be reviewed and checked first.
A separate Claude helper started for one job, such as building one session of the plan.
A GitHub setting that merges the pull request by itself once its checks pass.
A to-do item recorded on GitHub.
A saved snapshot of the code changes, with a message.

blocks.title: Things you might say that call for it
items: "implement the plan end to end"
"implement and raise a PR"
"finish this plan"
"take the plan to a PR"
"implement it all and merge"
any other way of asking for a plan to be built and shipped in one go rather than session by session

sections.heading: You answer every question once, at the start

blocks.title: The four questions
rows: Implementer model: which model builds the plan
Finalize model: which model runs finalize-pr's review and test-plan helpers
Git and merge: "Do you give permission in advance for the commits, the push and opening the PR, and should the PR auto-merge once checks pass?"
Yes, auto-merge (Recommended); Yes, stop at open PR; No, stop before pushing
UI audit: "If the implementation changes UI, run the UI audit?" Asked only when the `ui-audit` plugin is installed.

blocks.title: What each git and merge answer sets

blocks.text: Auto lets `/model-picker:pick-model` choose a model and effort for each session just before it starts, for building only, not finalize-pr. It adds a follow-up question, "Highest model auto may pick?" (No cap, Opus, Sonnet). A higher pick runs on the cap model with effort one level up.
With git permission No, Claude still builds the plan and commits on your machine, so nothing leaves it. It stops before the push and hands back to you.

sections.heading: Helpers build the plan and fix related problems on the way

before.label: Split plan
before.text: Claude runs /plan-tools:plan-split-implment. Sessions added during the run are picked up like any other.

after.label: Single plan
after.text: One helper builds the whole plan, committing as it goes. If the plan is clearly too big for one context, Claude runs /plan-tools:split-plan first and treats it as a split plan. If that helper ends with a question, Claude asks you and sends the answer back.

blocks.title: Rules every building helper follows
items: It uses the implementer model you chose.
A bug, gap or loose end related to the plan is fixed as part of the plan. No follow-up GitHub issue and no TODO for later.
If such a problem is too big for the current session, a new session file is added to the plan right after the current one.
Problems unrelated to the plan are left alone and mentioned in the final report.
Existing GitHub issues are never created, commented on, edited or closed.

blocks.title: Along the way
items: Claude makes sure the work is on a feature branch. On `main` or `master` it creates `plan/<feature-name>`, or uses the name you passed with `--branch`.
If building stops in a broken state, Claude stops and reports. It does not push a half-built plan.

sections.heading: finalize-pr runs once, and fixes things instead of filing them

cards.title: Your finalize model
cards.text: finalize-pr's helpers use the finalize model you chose.

cards.title: One test-plan pass
cards.text: It runs the test plan once, fixes what it finds and moves on.

cards.title: No follow-up issues
cards.text: Each unresolved item related to the plan is fixed by a helper and committed before the PR opens. Unrelated items go into the PR description under "Notes".

cards.title: No new questions
cards.text: Its push and UI-audit questions were already answered at the start, so it asks nothing.

blocks.text: With git permission No, finalize-pr stops before pushing and does not open the pull request.

sections.heading: With auto-merge chosen, Claude watches the PR until it merges

nodes.label: Auto-merge turned on
nodes.note: with a merge method the repo allows, squash if allowed

blocks.text: This step runs only when you chose auto-merge and gave git permission. With git permission No there is no pull request, so it is skipped.

sections.heading: You get a short report at the end

cards.title: Sessions run
cards.text: Including any added during the run.

cards.title: Unrelated notes
cards.text: Anything unrelated that was noted in the PR description.

reference.title: Default conventions
items: Plan work happens on a branch named `plan/<feature-name>`, shared with `plan-split-implment`. Change it with `--branch <name>`.
Helpers run on the `sonnet` model by default; plan-implement-complete asks you up front. Other skills set this their own way.

Auto-merge uses a merge method the repository allows: plan-implement-complete prefers squash, while monitor-pr asks when more than one is allowed. The repository's merge settings decide which are allowed.

reference.title: About the plan-tools plugin
items: Plugin purpose: plan-driven workflow tools that bootstrap a new web or mobile app end to end, split implementation plans into context-sized resumable sessions, and drive them to PRs.
Installing plan-tools also installs the plugins it depends on: `ntfy`, `fastapi-template` and `htmx-vs-alpine`.

No environment variables are needed. The one setting, `designer_ui_review` (default `false`), is changed with `/plugin configure plan-tools@wovemind`. When it is `true` and the `ui-change-guard` plugin is installed, finalize-pr runs `/ui-change-guard:review-ui-change` before it raises the PR, and labels the PR `ui-risky` if the review still finds a problem.
A default only takes effect after you open the settings dialog and save it once. Until then the setting counts as off.

next_action.text: Run /plan-tools:plan-implement-complete in the repo with your plan, and answer its four questions.
next_action.detail: After that one round it runs unattended, stopping only for real blockers.
